name: sort
ap_sql: SELECT k, c, pad FROM sbtest1 WHERE id <= 400000 ORDER BY c DESC, pad ASC, k DESC
desc: Sort 400K rows (~72MB) — spills at WM=64MB; SB=1024 creates IO baseline

name: io_join
ap_sql: SELECT s1.id, s1.k, s2.c, s2.pad FROM sbtest1 s1 JOIN sbtest2 s2 ON s1.id = s2.id ORDER BY s2.c DESC, s1.pad ASC
desc: Full JOIN sbtest1+sbtest2 (2M rows, ~920MB scan) — IO bottleneck at SB=1024MB

cardinality.note: GaussDB planner reports ~16.5M rows (8x overestimate) due to broken join cardinality estimation on PK-PK equi-join; override prevents WM over-allocation
